trial_court: learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, Raipur, Criminal Case No. 11222/2019
case_name: Smt. Indrani Sharma vs State Of Chhattisgarh

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Smt. Indrani Sharma, Parmanand Sharma, Abhishek Sharma, Ojaswini Sharma
parties.respondent_defendant: State Of Chhattisgarh, Smt. Saumya Sharma

facts_of_case: Marriage dispute between Abhishek Sharma and Smt. Saumya Sharma. FIR lodged against petitioners for offence under Section 498-A/34 of IPC. Charge-sheet filed before trial court.

legal_principles.principle: Criminal proceedings arising out of matrimonial disputes can be quashed by the Court if the matter has been settled between the parties amicably.
legal_principles.held: The Hon'ble Supreme Court held that in an identical circumstance, this Court held that the High Court in exercise of its inherent powers under Section 482 can quash criminal proceedings in matrimonial disputes where the dispute is entirely private and the parties are willing to settle their disputes amicably.
cited_cases: Jitendra Raghuvanshi and others vs. Babita Raghuwanshi and another, (2013) 4 SCC 58
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — in cases where parties have settled their disputes amicably

legal_principles.principle: If for the purpose of securing the ends of justice, quashing of FIR becomes necessary, Section 320 would not be a bar to the exercise of power of quashing.
legal_principles.held: This Court held that if for the purpose of securing the ends of justice, quashing of FIR becomes necessary, Section 320 would not be a bar to the exercise of power of quashing.
cited_cases: State of Haryana vs. Bhajan Lal, 1992 Supp (1) SCC 335
Pepsi Foods Ltd. & Anr. vs. Special Judicial Magistrate & Ors., (1998) 5 SCC 749
legal_principles.significance: MEDIUM — in cases where the FIR is unnecessary for securing the ends of justice

outcome.final_order: Criminal proceedings quashed in pursuance of compromise between parties.
